note: JSON:API Menu items exposes each menu's enabled, access-checked link tree as a read-only JSON:API resource at /%jsonapi%/menu_items/{menu} (route jsonapi_menu_items.menu, backed by MenuItemsResource on jsonapi_resources). No config, permissions, schema, services, or Drush. Query filters: min_depth, max_depth, parent, parents, conditions[]. Each item exposes title, url, route, weight, enabled, expanded, menu_name, parent, provider, options, description, meta (+ menu_link_content fields). Medium cases create a known menu/links and ask what the resource returns; hard cases build menu state (create a menu+link; enable a disabled link) so the resource returns it. Verify scripts reproduce the resource's own data source (menu.link_tree->load with onlyEnabledLinks + checkAccess/sort manipulators). All fixtures namespaced jmi_* menus.

evals.prompt: Using the jsonapi_menu_items module, what is the URL/path to fetch the link tree of a Drupal menu (say the 'main' menu) over JSON:API?
evals.expected_output: GET /%jsonapi%/menu_items/{menu}, e.g. /jsonapi/menu_items/main. It is served by route jsonapi_menu_items.menu (MenuItemsResource), returning the menu's enabled links as JSON:API resource objects.

evals.prompt: Which query filters does the jsonapi_menu_items resource support to limit which menu links are returned (e.g. by depth or parent)?
evals.expected_output: filter[min_depth], filter[max_depth], filter[parent] (a root plugin id), filter[parents] (comma-separated plugin ids), and filter[conditions][<field>][value|operator].

evals.prompt: What information does each menu item in a jsonapi_menu_items response include, and does it return disabled menu links?
evals.expected_output: Each item exposes attributes like title, url, route (name+parameters), weight, enabled, expanded, menu_name, parent, provider, options, description, meta (plus menu_link_content entity fields). Only enabled, access-checked links are returned; disabled links are omitted.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a menu with the machine name 'jmi_probe'. Using the jsonapi_menu_items resource for that menu (or by inspecting the running site), report the title of the menu link it returns.
evals.expected_output: The resource GET /jsonapi/menu_items/jmi_probe returns one item whose title attribute is 'JMI Probe Home' (an enabled menu_link_content link pointing to the front page).

evals.prompt: The menu 'jmi_vis' on this site contains two menu links, but the jsonapi_menu_items resource only returns some of them. Inspect the running site and state the title of the link that the resource returns for this menu.
evals.expected_output: Only 'JMI Visible' is returned. The resource uses MenuTreeParameters::onlyEnabledLinks(), so the disabled link 'JMI Hidden' is excluded from /jsonapi/menu_items/jmi_vis.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, set things up so that the jsonapi_menu_items resource for a menu named 'jmi_task' returns a menu link titled 'API Endpoint Link'. Create the menu 'jmi_task' and add an enabled link with that title pointing to the front page. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create a menu entity 'jmi_task' and a menu_link_content link (title 'API Endpoint Link', link internal:/, enabled) in it. Then GET /jsonapi/menu_items/jmi_task returns that link. Verified via the same menu.link_tree the resource uses (enabled + access-checked).

evals.prompt: On this site the menu 'jmi_edit' has a menu link called 'Toggle Link' that is currently disabled, so it does not appear in the site's JSON:API menu-items feed for that menu. Make that link show up in the feed. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Enable the 'Toggle Link' menu_link_content link in menu jmi_edit (set enabled = TRUE and save). The jsonapi_menu_items resource returns only enabled links, so once enabled it appears in /jsonapi/menu_items/jmi_edit. Verified via menu.link_tree onlyEnabledLinks + access check.
